card.name: Small linking words in drug-effect sentences
card.fires_on: Small linking words (a, of, in, no, the, parentheses) and verbs like maintain or inhibit that come just before a mechanism or effect term in drug-label text. The next word is often a noun such as efficacy, fractures or an enzyme-related term.

modes.label: Linking word before an effect
modes.description: Words like of, in or no right before a risk or efficacy outcome.
modes.example: increases the risk of GI toxicity, with little or no increase<< in>> efficacy [ see Warnings and Preca

modes.label: Verb before an action
modes.description: Verbs such as maintain or inhibit before an action on a target.
modes.example: Concurrent administration of antiviral drugs may<< inhibit>>

modes.label: Article in a definition
modes.description: A or the opening a description of a molecule or factor.
modes.example: through inhibition of the synthesis of N-acetylglutamate,<< a>> co-factor for carbamyl phosphate synth
